top_rules: Never pool virtual threads or wrap them in a fixed-size ExecutorService to throttle concurrency (JEP 444); use a Semaphore instead.

State synchronized-vs-ReentrantLock conditionally on JDK floor: migrate hot/blocking synchronized to ReentrantLock below JDK 24; default to synchronized on JDK 24+ per JEP 491's own JCIP-quoting guidance.

StructuredTaskScope/Joiner MUST NOT ship in published code while preview — enforced by JEP 12's class-file mechanism (preview bytecode only runs on the exact JDK feature release, with --enable-preview again at runtime), not just API instability.
Re-check the shipped-code guard against the JEP's own Status/Scope field (currently targeting JDK 28 finalisation), not on a fixed calendar.
jdk.tracePinnedThreads was removed in JDK 24 and silently does nothing — the only surviving pinning detector is the jdk.VirtualThreadPinned JFR event (default-enabled, 20ms threshold).

Bound fan-out at the real downstream resource's capacity (connection pool size, native library concurrency limit, API rate limit) with a Semaphore or bounded Joiner — never at 'thread count', since virtual threads removed the accidental platform-thread throttle.

Audit ThreadLocal-based per-thread caching before scaling onto virtual threads, but don't default to 'swap in a lock-free pool' — jackson-core tried that as a default (2.17.0) and reverted it (2.17.1) after production regressions.

Every rule row or code sample naming a concrete StructuredTaskScope/Joiner member must carry its JDK number — fork()'s return type, constructors-vs-factories, allSuccessfulOrThrow()'s return type, and onTimeout()/timeout() have each changed across JDK 21-27.
Prefer ScopedValue over ThreadLocal for one-way context into forked tasks; never pass a literal null to orElse — it now throws NullPointerException at runtime since JDK 25's finalisation.
'--enable-preview' is not a corpus norm (1/32, test-runtime only) — any rule recommending it must say so explicitly.
surprises: jackson-core changed its default BufferRecyclerPool from threadLocalPool() to a lock-free pool in 2.17.0, then reverted the default back in 2.17.1 after production regressions, and deprecated the lock-free pool entirely in 2.18.0 — the 'obvious' virtual-thread fix for ThreadLocal caching was tried by the flagship library itself and rolled back.

HikariCP maintainers left two independent PRs (2023, 2024) to replace internal synchronized with ReentrantLock for virtual-thread friendliness unmerged, and an open issue shows a real production report of JEP 491's documented 'still pins' class-initializer case on JDK 24.

Preview status is not just an API-stability warning: JEP 12's class-file mechanism means preview bytecode only loads on the exact JDK feature release that compiled it, with --enable-preview required again at runtime — a published SDK built against a preview API cannot be consumed cross-JDK at all, which is a much harder constraint than 'the API might change'.
fork() returning Subtask instead of Future is not a recent change — it's been true since the very first preview in JDK 21 (JEP 453), years before the brief's other version-sensitive changes.

micronaut-core's sole --enable-preview usage in the whole 32-repo corpus is scoped to the Test task's JVM args only, not the JavaCompile task for its main sourceset — the one corpus precedent for preview flags isn't even a production compile-time usage.

StructuredTaskScope became a sealed interface (not an abstract class) as early as JEP 525 (JDK 26), a detail rarely mentioned in older tutorials still describing it as a class with subclasses ShutdownOnFailure/ShutdownOnSuccess.

top_rules: Never install CoroutineExceptionHandler on anything but a root coroutine (direct child of CoroutineScope/supervisorScope/SupervisorJob) — on a nested coroutine it is silently never called.
CoroutineExceptionHandler has no effect on async — its exception only surfaces at .await(), so wrap await() in try/catch instead.

Rethrow CancellationException from every catch/runCatching before other handling — verify with detekt's SuspendFunSwallowedCancellation, which ships but is active:false by default and must be turned on explicitly.

GlobalScope is not an absolute ban: GlobalScope.launch(explicitParentContext, ...) carrying a real caller-owned Job is the one sanctioned exception; a bare GlobalScope.launch{}/.async{} is always the violation — detekt's GlobalCoroutineUsage flags both forms indiscriminately, so a human pass is still needed.

Dispatchers.IO defaults to max(64, cores) threads; limitedParallelism(n) views are elastic and share IO's own pool rather than allocating n new threads, so multiple views do not sum on top of the base ceiling.
@Volatile never fixes a shared-counter race (counter++ is read-modify-write, not atomic) — use AtomicInteger, coarse-grained thread confinement, or Mutex.withLock instead.

A long-running loop needs a suspension point or an isActive/ensureActive()/yield() check to be cancellable — confirmed there is genuinely no lint for this specific check, unlike GlobalScope/swallowed-cancellation which do have inactive-by-default detekt rules.

runTest's single-threaded virtual scheduler cannot reproduce a real thread-level data race; any concurrency-safety claim (atomics/confinement/mutex fixes) needs a separate real-dispatcher stress test alongside the runTest suite, not instead of it.
surprises: detekt already ships lint coverage for two of the brief's five MUST rows — GlobalCoroutineUsage (GlobalScope) and SuspendFunSwallowedCancellation — but both are active:false by default, so 'detekt is configured' does not mean these checks run; the brief's 'no lint exists' premise only holds for the missing-cooperative-cancellation-check row.

The exemplar corpus supplies a concrete, real-world instance of the GlobalScope exception the brief asks to decide: ktor's CIOEngine calls GlobalScope.launch(parentContext, ...), passing the caller's real Job so the coroutine is not actually detached — this is the shape a 'named exception' rule should codify.

Medium blocks every fetch method available (WebFetch, curl+UA, web.archive.org, freedium.cfd) with 403/DNS failures for both Elizarov design-rationale articles; had to fall back to search-engine-indexed verbatim excerpts, flagged explicitly in Sources as partial-confidence.

detekt also ships SuspendFunInFinallySection (inactive by default) and SleepInsteadOfDelay (active by default) that directly cover two more of this dive's normative candidates (NonCancellable-in-finally, and Thread.sleep on any dispatcher) — neither was anticipated by the brief.

detekt's coroutines rule classes now live under package dev.detekt.rules.coroutines rather than the historical io.gitlab.arturbosch.detekt.rules.coroutines, a rename that will break an agent's training-era assumptions about the group/package coordinates for custom detekt config.

top_rules: Every spawn point takes a constructor-injected ProcessLauncher interface — Java has no mockable process API, so this interface is the only test seam
Never fully drain stdout before touching stderr (or vice versa) without redirectErrorStream(true) — the JDK javadoc names this a deadlock risk on a full pipe buffer
Kill ladder is destroy() -> waitFor(grace) -> destroyForcibly() -> waitFor(), run unconditionally from a finally; on Windows destroy() is already forcible so the grace window is a no-op there
If the wrapped CLI can fork children, walk process.descendants() and destroy each handle — Process.destroy() never reaches descendants (no killpg equivalent on the JVM)

Use Process.onExit()'s CompletableFuture for the async path, not virtual threads — onExit costs nothing on the JDK floor (available since JDK 9) while virtual threads force a jump to JDK 21 for a fan-out regime this one-command-at-a-time SDK doesn't have
StructuredTaskScope must never appear in shipped SDK source — still preview through JDK 27, and a library can't force --enable-preview on consumers
ProcessBuilder.environment() starts as a live copy of System.getenv() — always .clear() before populating, or the ambient environment silently leaks into the child

Sysexit 75 is retried strictly before any exception is constructed, and retryability is a fixed no-argument property on the exception type itself, never threaded from a RetryPolicy, so it can't be skipped or forgotten at a call site
The 16-member exit-code enum is hand-maintained and diffed by a literal-set unit test against both ocx-sdk-python and rules_ocx/AGENTS.md — never generated from either
Read System.getenv() in exactly one classified OCX_ENV_CLASSES builder, never scattered across call sites, and never read the two explicit-class variables from the environment under any code path
surprises: The JVM has no killpg/process-group primitive at all — Process.destroy()/destroyForcibly() only ever reach the immediate child, so a kill ladder for a CLI that forks its own children needs an explicit Process.descendants() walk that ocx-sdk-python's POSIX process-group approach doesn't need to replicate

On Windows, Process.destroy() is already forcible (TerminateProcess) — there is no graceful-shutdown phase at all on that platform, so the entire grace-window rationale of the kill ladder is POSIX-only

java.net.http ships zero JSON support of any kind (BodyHandlers only return String/InputStream/Path) — the zero-runtime-dependency commitment's hand-rolled JSON reader isn't a corner being cut, it's the only option the JDK leaves open for parsing either HTTP bodies or captured CLI stdout

The 32-repo exemplar corpus has no exemplar at all for this row (M-Y-02 is 'partial' coverage sourced only from ocx-sdk-python) — the OCX SDK itself will be the fleet's first measured instance of this pattern, so every normative rule here is evidenced against prior art and JDK docs rather than a corpus library already doing it

Choosing virtual threads for this one boundary alone would force the SDK's JDK floor from the map's default 17 up to 21 — a four-major-version jump paid for a concurrency regime (high fan-out blocking-style I/O) this 'one command at a time' SDK never actually exercises

rule_ids: JAVA-CONC-01 — Never construct a fixed-size pool of virtual threads; bound concurrency with a Semaphore sized to the downstream resource.
JAVA-CONC-02 — Bound fan-out at the real downstream resource's capacity, never at the number of tasks.
JAVA-CONC-03 — State the synchronized-vs-ReentrantLock guidance conditionally on the module's JDK floor, split at JDK 24; never as one unconditional sentence.
JAVA-CONC-04 — Do not use -Djdk.tracePinnedThreads anywhere; use the jdk.VirtualThreadPinned JFR event as the only pinning detector on JDK 24+.
JAVA-CONC-05 — Keep StructuredTaskScope and every other preview API off the main-sourceset compile path of any published module.
JAVA-CONC-06 — Carry the verified JDK number on every code sample, comment or snippet naming a StructuredTaskScope/Joiner member, and re-read the member against that JDK's javadoc before emitting it.
JAVA-CONC-07 — Carry one-way context with ScopedValue rather than ThreadLocal, and never pass a literal null to ScopedValue.orElse.
JAVA-CONC-08 — Audit static ThreadLocal caches before scaling onto virtual threads, and state the chosen replacement strategy instead of blanket-swapping in a lock-free pool.
JAVA-CONC-09 — Take a ProcessLauncher by constructor injection at every CLI spawn point; never call new ProcessBuilder(...).start() outside the one real implementation.
JAVA-CONC-10 — Drain stdout and stderr concurrently; never read one to completion before touching the other.
JAVA-CONC-11 — Run the kill ladder destroy → waitFor(grace) → destroyForcibly → waitFor from a finally on every spawn path, walking descendants() when the CLI can fork.
JAVA-CONC-12 — Clear ProcessBuilder.environment() before writing to it, and read System.getenv() in exactly one classified env-table builder.
JAVA-CONC-13 — Use Process.onExit()'s CompletableFuture for the async path with an explicit bounded Executor on any blocking stage; do not adopt virtual threads here.
JAVA-CONC-14 — Retry sysexit 75 inside the spawn call before any exception is constructed, and expose retryability as a fixed no-argument property on the exception type.
KT-CORO-01 — Explicitly activate detekt's four inactive-by-default coroutine rules in the committed config; never treat 'detekt is applied' as evidence they run.
KT-CORO-02 — Fix every bare GlobalScope.launch/async; accept only the context-carrying adapter-boundary form that passes a Job the caller owns.
KT-CORO-03 — Never call runBlocking from inside a suspend fun.
KT-CORO-04 — Install a CoroutineExceptionHandler only on a root coroutine, never on async and never on a nested launch.
KT-CORO-05 — Rethrow CancellationException from every catch clause wide enough to observe it, runCatching included.
KT-CORO-06 — Keep unbounded or long-blocking work off bare Dispatchers.IO; give each blocking call site a limitedParallelism(n) view sized to the real resource.
KT-CORO-07 — Fix a shared-mutable-state race with atomics, coarse-grained confinement or Mutex.withLock, never with @Volatile.
KT-CORO-08 — Wrap any suspending call in a finally that must complete despite cancellation in withContext(NonCancellable).
KT-CORO-09 — Put a suspension point or an isActive/ensureActive() check in every long-running loop inside a coroutine body.
KT-CORO-10 — Inject the dispatcher in library and SDK code rather than hardcoding Dispatchers.IO/Default/Unconfined.
KT-CORO-11 — Add a real-dispatcher stress test alongside runTest for any test whose claim is thread safety.
KT-CORO-12 — Launch a coroutine that must outlive the test body on backgroundScope.
KT-CORO-13 — Choose StandardTestDispatcher for ordering-sensitive tests and UnconfinedTestDispatcher only when ordering is irrelevant.
conflicts_resolved: Virtual threads vs Process.onExit() for the SDK's async path — map conflict 13 said 'virtual threads, no reactive stack'; the process dive says onExit()'s CompletableFuture. Resolved for the process dive: conflict 13 rejected a reactive runtime, it did not mandate Thread.ofVirtual(); onExit() is JDK 9 and free on the floor of 17, while virtual threads would force 17 → 21 for a fan-out this one-command-at-a-time SDK never performs. JAVA-CONC-01/02 still govern wherever the fleet does fan out.

The --enable-preview grep scope — the process dive's check ('grep StructuredTaskScope|--enable-preview over build files must be empty') is over-broad and would flag micronaut-core's test-runtime jvmArg, the corpus's only precedent, as a violation. Resolved in favour of the VT dive's sourceset-scoped check: read which task the flag feeds; a compilerArgs entry on a published main sourceset is the violation, a Test{jvmArgs} entry is not. Same failure shape as the wave-2 correction to GRADLE-DEP-05.

'No lint exists for GlobalScope or swallowed CancellationException' (the KT-CORO brief's working assumption) vs detekt shipping both — resolved: both ship, and both are active:false by default, so 'detekt is configured' is not 'these checks run'. Re-measured across all 32 clones 2026-09-12: 1/32 activates any (detekt itself, GlobalCoroutineUsage only), 0/32 activate SuspendFunSwallowedCancellation or SuspendFunInFinallySection. Promoted to KT-CORO-01, the gate row.

GlobalScope: absolute ban vs named exception — detekt's GlobalCoroutineUsage flags both forms identically, and map row M-U-01's @OptIn(DelicateCoroutinesApi) grep is present on both too, so neither is a sufficient check. Resolved: the bare no-argument form is the MUST-fix; GlobalScope.launch(explicitParentContext, …) at an adapter boundary is structurally parented (ktor CIOEngine.kt:73) and is accepted. A finding is a question, never an automatic rewrite.

synchronized vs ReentrantLock — the widely-trained unconditional 'migrate to ReentrantLock to avoid pinning' formulation is provably wrong above JDK 24, where JEP 491 itself quotes JCIP §13.4 for defaulting to synchronized and says migrated code need not be reverted. Resolved as a floor-conditional rule with the split named at 24.

'limitedParallelism(n) views do not sum' read as 'do not create views' — resolved: creating views is cheap and correct (a LimitedDispatcher queues its own tasks onto IO's shared pool), the anti-pattern is unbounded blocking work on bare Dispatchers.IO. KT-CORO-06 targets the base dispatcher, not the view count.

Can runTest's virtual time hide a real race (the corpus's open Kotlin-testing question)? Resolved: yes, structurally — every TestDispatcher runs its queue one task at a time on a single scheduler thread, so a genuine data race or lock-ordering bug cannot fail there. A thread-safety claim needs a separate real-dispatcher massiveRun-shaped stress test; runTest stays default for suspension-order and cancellation logic.

The basis for the 'no StructuredTaskScope in shipped code' rule — API instability (map conflict 15) vs JEP 12's class-file mechanism (VT dive §6). Resolved to the more specific formulation: minor_version all-16-bits-set pins a preview class file to the exact feature release that compiled it, so a JDK-26-built jar will not run on JDK 27 even with --enable-preview re-passed. That makes the rule a technical constraint, not a maturity opinion.

top_rules: Never implement JavaToolchainResolver to provision a non-JDK CLI -- its request/response types are JDK-only with no checksum field

Provision a pinned binary via a BuildService registered from Plugin<Settings>.apply() with gradle.sharedServices.registerIfAbsent(...); download+sha256 happen inside the service's execution-time code, never in apply() or a ValueSource
Never enforce a sha256 check inside a ValueSource -- it can compute a hash but has no authority to fail a task; enforcement belongs in the BuildService
Cache the provisioned binary under GRADLE_USER_HOME keyed on its sha256, never under build/, so a cold-runner download amortizes across invocations
A Settings plugin's shared BuildService registration is IP-safe only if registered exactly once with parameters fixed at registerIfAbsent time and never mutated or enumerated afterward
Run Isolated Projects diagnostics (-Dorg.gradle.isolated-projects.diagnostics=true) periodically but never wire org.gradle.isolated-projects=true into a required CI gate
Ban two subprojects sharing a leaf path segment anywhere in the settings tree (gradle/gradle#847, open since 2016, no build failure to hang it on -- treat as MUST-fail-CI via a script)
Never place gradle.properties in a subproject directory -- org.gradle.* keys are read once from root/GRADLE_USER_HOME and silently never consulted per-subproject
Gate remote build-cache push on possession of a write credential, never on CI-ness or branch name alone -- a fork PR's run is also 'CI' but lacks injected secrets

Do not treat a JSR-305-to-JSpecify annotation swap on a plugin's public API as routine -- JSpecify defaults to strict/errors in Kotlin 2.1+ while JSR-305 only warns, so the swap can newly break consumers
surprises: Gradle's own docs say registering a shared BuildService via gradle.sharedServices.registerIfAbsent(...) is explicitly 'safe with Isolated Projects' -- the opposite of the brief's framing that this shape is IP-hostile by construction; the safety is bounded because two of IP's four constraint categories (cross-build, build-to-project access) are still 'not fully enforced yet' as of 9.7.0

JavaToolchainResolver itself extends BuildService<BuildServiceParameters.None>, and JavaToolchainDownload carries only a bare HTTPS URI to a zip/tar -- there is no checksum field anywhere in the toolchain-resolver contract, so even for genuine JDK provisioning Gradle's sanctioned seat never enforces a hash

gradle/gradle#847 (duplicate subproject leaf names) is still open and reproducing on Gradle 8.12.1 as of a 2025-06-30 comment, with zero fix across the 8.x or 9.x lines despite 137 reactions since 2016

No corpus settings file gates remote build-cache push on credential possession except testcontainers-java; detekt's seemingly-careful isCiBuild-only gate is not actually fork-PR-safe, since fork PRs also run under CI

Kafka's build-scan gate (publishing.onlyIf { it.authenticated }) is a different Develocity feature (build scan, not cache) that just happens to be the map-cited exemplar shape -- its own buildCache{} block sidesteps the push question by disabling remote push outright rather than gating it

JSpecify defaulting to strict/errors in Kotlin (since 2.1) while JSR-305 stays warn-only makes the JSpecify migration the compatibility-risk direction, exactly backwards from an agent's likely instinct that adopting the newer spec-blessed annotation set is the safe upgrade

rule_ids: GRADLE-PLUG-22 — Never implement JavaToolchainResolver or add a toolchainManagement javaRepositories entry to provision a non-JDK tool (MUST).

GRADLE-PLUG-23 — Provision a pinned external binary from a BuildService registered once by gradle.sharedServices.registerIfAbsent in Plugin<Settings>.apply(), downloading in the service's execution-time method (MUST).
GRADLE-PLUG-24 — Enforce the sha256 by throwing from execution-time code before the binary reaches any classpath or PATH; never compute a hash for enforcement in a ValueSource (MUST).
GRADLE-PLUG-25 — Cache the provisioned binary under GRADLE_USER_HOME or a tool home, never under build/, and key the skip on the expected sha256 rather than file presence (MUST).
GRADLE-PLUG-26 — Set a shared BuildService's parameters inline at registerIfAbsent and never mutate them afterwards; read the service back only through findByName (MUST).
GRADLE-PLUG-27 — Run Isolated Projects diagnostics against the plugin's functional-test build once per release, and never wire org.gradle.isolated-projects=true into a required CI job (SHOULD).
GRADLE-PLUG-28 — Do not treat replacing JSR-305 with JSpecify annotations on a plugin's exported types as routine; it needs a major version and a migration note (MUST).
GRADLE-STRUCT-10 — Never create two projects sharing a path leaf segment in a build that also assigns a uniform explicit group (MUST).
GRADLE-STRUCT-11 — Never put an org.gradle.* key in a gradle.properties that is not the root of a build (MUST).
GRADLE-STRUCT-12 — Gate remote build-cache push on a write credential read through providers.environmentVariable(...).isPresent, never on CI-ness or a raw System.getenv (MUST).

top_rules: MUST: state immutability first — a PUBLISHED component can never be removed/updated/re-signed, only a new version recovers
MUST: fail the release job when git tag != declared build-file version, before any build step (0/32 exemplars enforce this any other way; mirror ocx-sdk-python's release.yml check verbatim)
MUST: verify namespace (DNS TXT or io.github.* GitHub ownership) as a precondition, not discovered as an upload failure
MUST: every artifact ships sources jar + javadoc jar + .md5 + .sha1 + .asc; POM needs name/description/url/licenses/developers/scm or Central rejects the whole upload

MUST: set autoPublish=true + waitUntil=published (or vanniktech automaticRelease/nmcp publishingType=AUTOMATIC) if a CI green check is meant to mean 'this is live on Central' — waitUntil=validated still needs a human click

MUST: never write mavenLocal() into a committed repositories{} block — Gradle's own docs call it reproducibility-breaking, 'restricted to prototyping'; publishToMavenLocal as a producer-side verification task is fine and unaffected

SHOULD not MUST: never write literal credentials{} values — on Gradle 9.0+ (fixed by gradle/gradle#33830, merged 2025-06-13) this silently disables the config cache for that task rather than failing as it did on 8.x; verify via the literal 'Reusing configuration cache.' line on a second run

CONSIDER not MUST: actions/attest-build-provenance for SLSA L2 is a rule this program introduces deliberately — 0/32 exemplars including bazelbuild/bazel and gradle/gradle use any provenance/scanning tooling, so state this explicitly rather than presenting it as observed practice
surprises: The two Gradle doc pages the brief named for mavenLocal() (declaring_repositories.html, best_practices_dependencies.html) say NOTHING about it — the actual warning ('restricted to prototyping rather than production builds') lives on a third, unnamed page: declaring_repositories_basics.html

The maven-publish/config-cache question resolves cleanly: gradle/gradle#33830 (merged 2025-06-13, milestone 9.0.0 RC1) changed the failure mode from a hard build failure (Gradle 8.x) to silent config-cache disablement (Gradle 9.0+) for exactly one shape — literal inline credentials{} — not a broad plugin incompatibility

0/32 exemplars use any git-tag-driven version plugin at all, which makes the ocx-sdk-python-style tag-vs-version CI check strictly necessary rather than a nice-to-have, since nothing else in observed practice enforces that consistency
Central's own placeholder-jar fallback for sources/javadoc (a jar containing just a README) is documented and sanctioned, not an anti-pattern to flag
3/32 exemplars still reference oss.sonatype.org URLs nearly a year after OSSRH's 2025-06-30 shutdown — live evidence of the exact AI-hallucination trap the corpus itself preserves

Sonatype's own Sigstore announcement states 'we have no intention of replacing PGP signatures' at launch, while also leaving the door open to eventually requiring both — there is no scheduled PGP deprecation to warn about

top_rules: Every published POM must declare name/description/url/licenses/developers/scm inside an explicit pom{} block — none is Gradle-property-derived and Central rejects an upload missing any.
Never propose maven.consumer.pom.flatten or <packaging>bom</packaging> as shipping mechanism — Maven 4.0.0 is still rc-6 on Central as of 2026-09-12; query the registry to re-check.

Any Gradle-only variant (feature variant, KMP target, Shadow's shadowRuntimeElements) is invisible to Maven and Bazel/Coursier by design — republish as a classified artifact if non-Gradle consumers need it.

To exclude a dependency from a shaded jar while keeping it correctly in the published POM, use Shadow's built-in `shadow` configuration — it has done this automatically since Shadow 1.1.0 (2014), no pom.withXml needed.

Ship a maven-consumability verification module (a small pom.xml + one smoke test resolving the published coordinates) rather than a second production build system — this is the corpus's actual dagger/okhttp/grpc-java/Exposed/junit-framework pattern.

A repo carrying both build.gradle* and pom.xml is a false-positive dual-build signal 10/10 times in this corpus — read the directory name (maven-tests/, examples/maven/, tooling-support-tests/) before concluding anything.

Scope GMM suppression to the one shaded module (kafka's tasks.withType(GenerateModuleMetadata){enabled=false} inside project(':clients')), never build-wide, since GMM costs Maven/Bazel nothing and gives Gradle consumers free variant-aware resolution.
Never disable Shadow's addShadowVariantIntoJavaComponent without a stated configuration-timing reason — it only controls a Gradle-only GMM variant that Maven/Bazel consumers never saw anyway.

top_rules: Pin all four version flags explicitly (--java_language_version/--java_runtime_version, --tool_java_language_version/--tool_java_runtime_version); never rely on Bazel's 11/local_jdk/11/remotejdk_11 defaults.
Prefer remotejdk_* over local_jdk for --java_runtime_version — local_jdk makes output depend on the build machine's installed JVM.
Express a below-toolchain bytecode target with --javacopt="-source N -target N", never by lowering --java_language_version, which also re-selects the java_toolchain via source_version matching.

Never set forcibly_disable_header_compilation=True without a recorded reason, and never call header compilation "ijar-based" — the default toolchain's header compiler is turbine (TurbineDirect), which parses source directly, not a compiled-jar stripper.

Confirm the strict-deps flag's real name on your own pinned binary before using it — command-line-reference says --experimental_strict_java_deps, user-manual says --strict_java_deps; only the experimental-prefixed spelling has exemplar evidence (rules_jvm_external).
Do not read an absent strict-deps flag as "unenforced" — default/strict/error are behaviorally identical and that is the behavior when the flag is unset; only off/warn weaken it.
Wire Error Prone severity via --javacopt="-Xep:Check:SEVERITY" or java_package_configuration+package_group — never as a maven/bazel_dep artifact, since error-prone ships no Bazel config of its own.

When multiple JVM registrations match the same OS/CPU, Bazel silently picks the first one registered, not the most specific — order register_toolchains() calls deliberately and comment the intended winner.
surprises: Bazel's own docs disagree on the strict-deps flag's name: command-line-reference calls it --experimental_strict_java_deps, user-manual calls it --strict_java_deps with no prefix — could not be resolved against a real bazel binary (none installed in the sandbox).

Strict Java deps is not something you turn on: per user-manual, default/strict/error are the same behavior and that IS the behavior when the flag is unset — an absent strict-deps line does not mean unenforced.

Header compilation on the default toolchain is turbine (TurbineDirect), not ijar — bazel-and-java's own prose only names ijar in that section, which misdescribes the mechanism (ijar strips a compiled jar; turbine parses source directly, no javac back-end invoked).
google/error-prone ships literally no MODULE.bazel/WORKSPACE/BUILD file at all; it's wired into Bazel purely via JavaBuilder + --javacopt/java_package_configuration, never as a dependency.

bazel-and-java's own page states the 'default javac options' are -source 8 -target 8, directly contradicting its own (and user-manual's) stated --java_language_version default of 11 two paragraphs apart — an internal doc inconsistency, not a live default.
contrib_rules_jvm's lint wrappers ARE bzlmod-native (own MODULE.bazel uses a `linter` module extension), but zero of the 32 program exemplars adopt them or apple_rules_lint at all.

top_rules: Set fail_if_repin_required = True on every maven.install — its default False leaves both lock-file self-checks (input-artifacts hash and resolved-artifacts hash) as warnings the build survives, unlike crate_universe's unconditional hard-fail.

Never hand-merge or line-merge maven_install.json — it has no safe human-editable region at all (unlike MODULE.bazel.lock's registryFileHashes); on conflict, resolve MODULE.bazel and regenerate wholesale via REPIN=1 bazel run @maven//:pin.
Never point Bazel's own bazel-lockfile-merge jq driver at maven_install.json — it parses MODULE.bazel.lock's schema, not this one; the two lockfiles must never be conflated in review or tooling.

Resolve every Kotlin coordinate through rules_jvm_external's maven.install, never a hand-rolled java_import — its generated jvm_import auto-detects kotlin_module entries and skips ijar, which otherwise strips inline-function bodies; the fix (PR #69, 2019) predates every currently-supported release.

In a repo that also builds the same Kotlin sources with Gradle, set kt_kotlinc_options(x_lambdas = "indy") explicitly — rules_kotlin's own default ("class") diverges from both Kotlin 2.x's compiler default and Gradle's default (both "indy"), producing different bytecode for identical source.

Set version_conflict_policy = "pinned" for deterministic resolution; reuse jvm-dependencies.md GRADLE-DEP-09 — this only decides which version wins a conflict, it never vets legitimacy, exactly like a lockfile.

Set strict_visibility = True on maven.install once a repo has more than a handful of contributors touching the artifacts list, so pruning it fails loudly instead of breaking an undeclared consumer later.

The dual-build Gradle+Bazel source-of-truth question (M-X-07) gets a reading heuristic only — require a canonical-build sentence in CONTRIBUTING/README, never invent a parity generator nothing in the corpus supports.
surprises: No merge between bazel-contrib/rules_jvm_external and bazel-contrib/rules_jvm has happened (both remain live, separate, non-archived repos) — but rules_kotlin itself underwent a GitHub org transfer from bazelbuild/ to bazel-contrib/, which is likely what the recent-shifts scout half-detected.

rules_jvm_external's freshness gate is NOT unconditional like crate_universe's: fail_if_repin_required defaults to False (confirmed in coursier.bzl source), so a stale or even hand-corrupted maven_install.json is merely a printed warning and the build still succeeds unless that flag is explicitly set — the opposite failure-mode shape from BZL-RUST-01.

The lock file self-checks on two independent hash fields, not one: __INPUT_ARTIFACTS_HASH (declared-vs-lock drift) and __RESOLVED_ARTIFACTS_HASH (lock-body self-tamper/bad-merge check) — both gated by the same fail_if_repin_required flag.

The ijar/Kotlin-inline-function bug is ancient (filed and fixed in 2019, PR #69) — there is no live rules_jvm_external version lacking the fix, so no version-floor caveat is actually needed for a repo starting today.

dagger already does almost everything right: fail_if_repin_required=True and lock_file are both set (MODULE.bazel:185-186), yet it still never sets version_conflict_policy or x_lambdas — showing the gate/pin discipline and the conflict-policy/codegen discipline are adopted completely independently in practice.

No exemplar in the corpus (0/6 Bazel-carrying repos, including dagger's dual Gradle+Bazel Kotlin build) sets x_lambdas at all — the silent-default bytecode divergence is not hypothetical, it's the observed universal state.

conflicts_resolved: ijar vs turbine, between the two dives — the toolchains dive says the default toolchain's header compiler is turbine and 'ijar-based' is a misdescription; the deps/Kotlin dive says ijar strips Kotlin inline-function bodies. Resolved by scope split: turbine parses SOURCE for java_library/kt_jvm_library, ijar strips a PREBUILT jar for java_import. Neither rule cures the other's failure — forcibly_disable_header_compilation does not fix the Kotlin trap, and routing Kotlin through maven.install does not change the header compiler. Both survive as separate rules (BZL-JAVA-07, BZL-JAVA-18) plus one merged failure mode.

Strict-deps severity and spelling — the toolchains dive made 'confirm the flag name on your own pinned binary' a MUST whose verification cannot run without a bazel binary (this program has none, and an adopting agent often will not either). Resolved by splitting: BZL-JAVA-05 demoted to SHOULD with the exemplar-evidenced spelling (--experimental_strict_java_deps, rules_jvm_external@449754dcbb:.bazelrc:9) as the writable default, and the MUST moved to BZL-JAVA-04, the misreading that licenses a real edit (absent flag already means error, so 'not enforced here' ends in =off).

strict_visibility severity — the deps dive rated it CONSIDER on 'absent is a finding to raise, not an automatic block'. Promoted to SHOULD (BZL-JAVA-13) on re-measurement: three of the four exemplars carrying a real external Maven graph set it (bazel@948b8c70e2:MODULE.bazel:269, grpc-java@fc4314419d:MODULE.bazel:78,100, rules_jvm_external@449754dcbb:MODULE.bazel:86), and it is the only mechanism that fails an undeclared transitive use at the point of the edit.

fail_if_repin_required — who actually violates. The deps dive's exemplar table named only dagger (satisfies) and grpc-java (violates by absence), implying the careful repos set it. Re-measured here: bazel-contrib__rules_jvm_external@449754dcbb:MODULE.bazel:81-86 — the ruleset that SHIPS the flag sets lock_file and strict_visibility on its own primary maven.install and not the gate (it does set it on a test fixture at :506-507). MUST stands; the violation row is now named.

M-X-08 / _deploy.jar — the toolchains dive deferred it wholly to jvm-distribution.md DIST-02..DIST-11 and emitted no BZL-JAVA rule. Resolved: the shading taxonomy is correctly inherited, but there is Bazel-only residue that file cannot carry — per bazel.build/reference/be/java, name_deploy.jar is an implicit output 'only built if explicitly requested', so a green bazel build //... never builds the shipped artifact. Ships as BZL-JAVA-21, MUST for CLI/application consumers.

x_lambdas and dagger — the deps dive filed dagger's unset x_lambdas under 'silent-default territory… not a counterexample'. Sharpened to a confirmed violation: dagger-compiler/main/java/dagger/internal/codegen/kotlin/BUILD:22-28 globs *.kt through compat_kt_jvm_library (tools/bazel_compat.bzl:20-26 → rules_kotlin's kt_jvm_library) while dagger-compiler/build.gradle.kts:6-10 applies kotlinJvm over source dirs wired to the same main/java tree (buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/dagger/gradle/build/DaggerConventionPlugin.kt:158-168). BZL-JAVA-03 — Express a below-toolchain bytecode target as --javacopt="-source N -target N" on an unchanged modern --java_language_version, never by lowering the language flag, which also re-selects the toolchain. (MUST)

top_rules: Never invoke `mvn integration-test` or `mvn clean install` as the CI gate — use `mvn verify`; hyphenated phases skip teardown/reporting and can hang containers.
State every Maven-4 claim with the re-check command (`curl .../maven-core/maven-metadata.xml`) inline — 4.0.0 has never shipped, only rc-6.
Set `<release>` on maven-compiler-plugin; unset `source`/`target` silently default to Java 8 regardless of the running JDK.
Query Central's maven-metadata.xml for Surefire, never the plugin doc-site's version banner — banner says 3.6.0, GA line is 3.5.6.

Flag any `.mvn/maven.config` using `aether.checksums.algorithms`/`aether.connector.smartChecksums` (resolver-1.x names) on a project whose wrapper pins Maven 4 — resolver 2.0 renamed both properties and the old names silently no-op.

Never present Maven checksum config as a security control — Maven Resolver's own docs state checksums are integrity-only and do not defend against MITM/supply-chain tampering; GPG signing is the trust layer.
Set `includeantruntime="false"` explicitly on every live `<javac>` before any other Ant migration work — same-system, zero-risk, Ant's own manual recommends it.
Never recommend `ant.importBuild()` as an end-state or default bridge — it disables the Gradle configuration cache for the whole build unconditionally, and 0/32 corpus repos use it for real.
surprises: assertj's `.mvn/maven.config` checksum flags are Maven-Resolver-1.x property names (correct for its pinned Maven 3.9.16/resolver 1.9.27) but resolver 2.0 (Maven 4) renamed both — the config silently becomes a no-op the day the wrapper moves to Maven 4, with no error at all.

Maven Resolver's own docs explicitly reject the 'MD5/SHA-1 are insecure' framing for Maven: checksums provide integrity only, never security/trust/MITM protection — the Gradle-verification-metadata mental model doesn't transfer.

`smartChecksums` only ever validates SHA-1 via an HTTP ETag header shortcut — leaving it on with a SHA-512-first algorithm list configures a stronger digest that never actually gets exercised; disabling it (as assertj does) is the operative half of the config, not the algorithm list.

Maven has no equivalent of Gradle's verification-metadata.xml at all — no file, plugin, or built-in feature plays that role; the closest levers (resolver checksum properties, GPG signing) are orthogonal, not substitutes.

apache/maven's own PR fixing the JDK17+ --add-opens/JaCoCo argLine clobber (apache/maven#11605) is still open and unmerged as of 2026-09-12 — the brief's cited bug has a proposed fix, not a shipped one.
The one wrapper-checksum exemplar in the whole corpus (assertj) sets neither wrapperSha256Sum nor distributionSha256Sum — 0/1, not partial adoption.

conflicts_resolved: jackson-databind's `argLine`: the dive recorded `FasterXML__jackson-databind@a906e1782b:pom.xml:44` as SATISFYING the JaCoCo-composition rule. Re-measured this consolidation — it VIOLATES it. `:44-46` is two bare `--add-opens` flags with no `@{argLine}` placeholder while `:212-215` binds jacoco-maven-plugin; the POM carries its own smoking gun at `:51-54` (`<jacocoStrict>false</jacocoStrict>`, comment "For some reason, release fails due to missing jacoco... so disable for now") and a consequently non-failing `requireFilesExist` on `target/jacoco.exec` at `:226-243`. The corpus's counterexample, not its exemplar.

`mvn verify` vs `install`: the dive stated a flat prohibition (candidate #2, carried from map row M-J-10 unmeasured). Measured the 5 Maven-primary repos' CI this consolidation: `google__guava@5fb424c43a:.github/workflows/ci.yml:53,56` runs a deliberate `-DskipTests install` reactor bootstrap and then gates on `verify` — correct. Resolved: the rule binds the GATE, not every invocation. The real violation is `google__error-prone@c1f99ad5d3:.github/workflows/ci.yml:88,91` (`mvn install -DskipTests` then `mvn test`), which never reaches `verify` at all.

Surefire version: map row M-J-08 says "3.6.0-M1", the dive's candidate #7 quotes the doc banner "3.6.0 / Last Published 2026-08-31", frame correction 38 says Central GA tops at 3.5.6. Resolved in favour of Central: MVN-BUILD-05 pins from `maven-metadata.xml` and describes the single-provider consolidation as a 3.6.0-line change not yet GA — a rule quoting the banner instructs an agent to pin a milestone as stable.

Family routing for the supply-chain rows: the dive routed them to MVN-DEP (it was commissioned to close jvm-dependencies.md's open "Maven-side checksum and verification policy" question). But the map routes MVN-DEP to `dependencies.md`, triggered by "adding a dependency"; an agent editing `.mvn/maven.config` or `maven-wrapper.properties` is editing build configuration. Resolved: they land in MVN-BUILD (family follows file kind); MVN-DEP-01…11 stand unchanged and are cited, not duplicated.

Internal tension in the dive: candidate #12 says Maven checksums are never a security control, candidate #14 makes the wrapper checksum a supply-chain MUST. Resolved by scope, both survive — Resolver checksums verify an artifact fetched inside a chain GPG can also cover (integrity only), whereas the wrapper checksum pins a distribution downloaded and executed before any trust chain exists and where no signature is ever checked, so integrity is the only available control there.

`.mvn/extensions.xml` is 0/32 per the shape audit §1 — but `apache__maven@ea4a417bd2:.github/workflows/maven.yml:77,93-95` copies one in before the Maven-3 leg and swaps it to `~/.m2/extensions.xml` for the Maven-4 leg. Resolved: the census counted committed files; an extension can replace the local repository wholesale, so MVN-BUILD-15 requires reading CI configs, not only `git ls-tree`.

Ant severity: map decision 3 folds Ant into a depth file because recognise-and-migrate fails rule-distillation's "it changes a diff" test; the dive proposes MUST-grade rules. Resolved: MVN-ANT rows ship as conditional-entry rules that fire only when a `build.xml` is in the diff. MVN-ANT-02 earns a MUST at 0/32 adoption because its blast radius is whole-build configuration-cache loss on the *Gradle* side, not on Ant.
needs_another_round: Maven compilation under modern JDKs — does a modern JDK disable implicit annotation processing by default, and must a Maven build set `<maven.compiler.proc>full</maven.compiler.proc>` for processors to run at all? `apache__maven@ea4a417bd2:pom.xml:135` sets it; no dive covered the javac mechanism, and a wrong rule makes an agent believe processors ran when they did not. Highest-value gap in the family.

Maven toolchains — what is the Maven-side equivalent of the toolchain-vs-`--release` split JAVA-PLAT owns for Gradle: `~/.m2/toolchains.xml`, `maven-toolchains-plugin`, or the `setup-java` matrix? `google__guava@5fb424c43a:.github/workflows/ci.yml:53,56` passes `-Dtoolchain.skip` and `-Dsurefire.toolchain.version`, implying a live toolchain configuration no audit read.

`maven-antrun-plugin` — Ant inside Maven: what does a rule say about `<target>`/`<tasks>` blocks embedded in a POM, the one Ant surface that appears in live Maven builds rather than legacy files? The map's Ant brief named the plugin; the dive never fetched it, and MVN-ANT as written only fires on a `build.xml`.

Maven build extensions as a resolution mechanism — does MVN-BUILD-15 become a MUST, and what does a rule say about an extension that replaces the local repository for CI only (apache/maven's Mimir)? Measured 0/32 committed, which is exactly why the CI-injected case was missed.

top_rules: JAVA-PLAT-01: toolchain and --release/.release are two separate declared values — never let sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility or <source>/<target> stand in for --release
JAVA-PLAT-02: SDK/library ships module-info.java with exports = exactly the public packages; Automatic-Module-Name only when floor <9 or module can't host sources, and it gives zero encapsulation
JAVA-PLAT-04: no global reflective-access relax flag since JDK 17 — every --add-opens/--add-exports is per-module, declared and commented at the call site
JAVA-PLAT-05: run jdeps --jdk-internals -R and jdeprscan --for-removal against every published artifact before any JDK-major bump; any hit blocks, doesn't just warn

JAVA-PLAT-06: before raising the CI matrix past JDK 21, grep every List/Deque/Set/Map/Collection implementor for a self-declared getFirst/getLast/addFirst/addLast/removeFirst/removeLast/reversed (SequencedCollection collision)
JAVA-PLAT-08: bind japicmp/BCV to check/verify directly (tasks.check.dependsOn / <phase>verify</phase>) — never leave it as a manual-only task or a CI-workflow-only side gate
JAVA-PLAT-10: before jspecifyMode = true, confirm JDK 22+ (any vendor) or 21.0.8+/17.0.19+ on an OpenJDK-family distro with -XDaddTypeAnnotationsToSymbol=true — never Oracle JDK 17/21 with the flag
JAVA-PLAT-11: OCX SDK floor is 17 (confirmed, matches Spring Boot 4 / JUnit 6), toolchain 25, CI matrix 17/21/25 — module-info.java needs no MR-JAR layer at this floor since it's already ≥9
surprises: Of the six declared japicmp adopters, only three (maven, gradle/gradle, testcontainers-java) bind the checker into the default build lifecycle — grpc-java's own build-file comment says 'Run with: ./gradlew japicmp --continue' (manual only), assertj only breaks the build inside a dedicated GitHub Actions workflow, and micronaut-core's check-binding lives in an external plugin repo not present in the sparse checkout

micronaut-core's accepted-breaks file is a much lighter template than gradle/gradle's: a flat {type, member, reason} JSON array (1370 lines) consumed via the japicmp-gradle-plugin's own richReport{addViolationTransformer(...)} extension point, not a custom ViolationRule class hierarchy — but the transformer class itself still has to be hand-written, it isn't shipped by the plugin
Because the OCX SDK's floor is already 17 (≥9), it needs none of guava's multi-release-JAR complexity for module-info.java — that indirection is strictly a floor-below-9 problem

gradle/gradle's own Kotlin-DSL build is the SequencedCollection worked example, not a satisfier of any rule: gradle/gradle#27699 is still open with no code fix, only 'avoid the colliding name' as workaround

NullAway's jspecifyMode JDK-vendor split is sharper than a version check: JDK 22+ works on any vendor including Oracle, but below 22 the flag is OpenJDK-family only (Temurin/Zulu) and literally does nothing on Oracle JDK 17/21 — and NullAway ≥0.12.11 throws IllegalStateException rather than degrading silently
JEP 493 (jlink without JMODs) is confirmed a JDK-vendor build-time opt-in (--enable-linkable-runtime), not a JDK-24+ guarantee — jlink --help's own enabled/disabled line is the only way to know

top_rules: Never call a charset-less overload (new String(byte[]), getBytes(), FileReader, PrintStream(OutputStream)) without an explicit Charset, even on JDK 18+ — JEP 400 changed the default value, not the API surface; verify with Error Prone DefaultCharset + SpotBugs DM_DEFAULT_ENCODING

Set org.gradle.jvmargs=-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 whenever CI/dev touches a non-UTF-8-default host, regardless of JDK floor — the daemon launches before toolchain selection and Gradle never sets file.encoding itself (gradle/gradle#2270, open)
Treat any file.encoding value other than UTF-8 or COMPAT on JDK 18+ as a defect — JEP 400's own spec note declares other values unspecified

Pin options.encoding/project.build.sourceEncoding explicitly regardless of JDK floor — a separate fallback point from JEP 400; only 15/32 exemplars set it, a different set from the 13/32 setting -Dfile.encoding

shadowJar inherits Gradle 9's reproducibleFileOrder/preserveFileTimestamps automatically — verified via source (ShadowJar never overrides createCopyActionExecuter, so AbstractArchiveTask's own logic drives file-tree order upstream of Shadow's custom CopyAction); do not add a redundant reproducibility block to shadowJar

mergeServiceFiles() preserves entry order deterministically but as classpath-resolution order (a LinkedHashSet in ServiceFileTransformer.kt), not sorted — byte-identical shadowJar output needs locked dependency versions, not just archive flags

Properties.store() always writes an unconditional timestamp comment line independent of archive-level fixes — strip via java.properties.date (Maven) or a comment-free/sorted Properties subclass (Shadow's own ReproducibleProperties is the reference shape)

Keep test-timezone pinning at CONSIDER only (0/32 corpus support) — jvm-quality-gates.md verdict 10 already names this as exactly what an agent invents unprompted; do not promote it to MUST/SHOULD without an owner decision
surprises: Shadow's ShadowJar never overrides Gradle's createCopyActionExecuter(), so Gradle 9's reproducibleFileOrder guarantee reaches shadowJar output for free, upstream of Shadow's entirely custom CopyAction/ZipOutputStream implementation — the two mechanisms (Gradle-level order, Shadow-level timestamp) are separate and answer the wave-2 handover question directly

Shadow already ships its own fix for the exact Properties.store() timestamp-comment bug this dive was asked to flag at the JDK level (internal/ReproducibleProperties.kt: overrides store() to throw, sorts entries, exposes writeWithoutComments()) — proof the bug is real and a template for the fix, found in a repo nobody expected to cite for this

mergeServiceFiles() merges into a Kotlin mutableSetOf() (LinkedHashSet), so merged META-INF/services line order is classpath-resolution order, not alphabetically sorted — Shadow's own docs don't state this either way, it required reading ServiceFileTransformer.kt directly

JEP 400's own text states 'no intent to deprecate or remove' charset-less overloads — the fix is entirely in Charset.defaultCharset()'s value, meaning new String(byte[])/getBytes() are just as charset-less and just as lint-worthy on JDK 25 as on JDK 8, despite usually being 'correct' now

kafka's build.gradle:362-364 copies Gradle's own pre-9 legacy-revert snippet verbatim while running wrapper 9.7.1 — an active, uncommented total opt-out of reproducibility that also silently negates whatever shadowJar in that same repo would otherwise inherit for free

Maven's Reproducible-Builds-by-default only starts at 4.0.0-beta-5, and Central's newest 4.x artifact is still 4.0.0-rc-6 as of 2026-09-12 — so 'Maven 4 does this automatically' is a claim about an unreleased line, not the corpus's actual Maven baseline

top_rules: Never emit -Xwhen-guards/-Xnon-local-break-continue/-Xmulti-dollar-interpolation/-Xcontext-parameters on Kotlin >=2.2.0/>=2.4.0 — they're silent no-ops, verify by grepping freeCompilerArgs against the pinned Kotlin version.
Never write -Xjvm-default=... on Kotlin >=2.2.0 — use the typed jvmDefault DSL property instead.
A Kotlin build upgrading to 2.2.0+ must set jvmDefault=DISABLE explicitly if it needs pre-2.2.0 binary-compat semantics — the default silently flipped to ENABLE.
Always set compilerOptions.jvmTarget explicitly alongside jvmToolchain(N) — the toolchain only back-fills jvmTarget when unset, and jvmTarget still defaults to "1.8".
jvmTargetValidationMode defaults to ERROR (hard fail), not WARNING — don't assume a soft warning on Kotlin/Java target mismatch.
Pin KGP version against the versioned Gradle/AGP compatibility table before bumping either — e.g. KGP 2.4.0-2.4.10 caps at Gradle 9.5.0/AGP 9.1.0.
New Kotlin modules needing an annotation processor must default to KSP; kapt is acceptable only when the specific processor has no KSP implementation, named in a comment.

Kover's check task DOES depend on koverVerify by default since Kover 0.7.0 (opposite of JaCoCo) — confirmed via github.com/Kotlin/kotlinx-kover/issues/523's task-dependency tree and maintainer's onCheck=false fix; this settles the wave-2 KT-TEST blocker.
Dokka floor should be pinned at >=2.2.0 using the DGP v2 top-level dokka{} extension, not the v1 per-task tasks.dokkaHtml{} shape.
Treat extraWarnings/-Wextra as a recommendation only — it has stayed Experimental through 2.1.0-2.4.0 with no stabilization signal.
surprises: Kover's own DSL reference (0.9.8) genuinely never states the check/koverVerify default anywhere — the definitive answer came from a closed GitHub issue's literal Gradle task-dependency tree plus a maintainer's onCheck=false reply, not from any doc sentence.

kapt in the exemplar corpus (google/dagger) is not legacy cruft being phased out — it's a deliberately preserved regression-test fixture (javatests/artifacts/**) proving the old Android/Hilt kapt path still works, while the real library modules are already KSP-only.

ktorio/ktor's own gradle.properties contains an in-repo comment explaining a genuine Kotlin-daemon-precedence gotcha: -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options nested inside org.gradle.jvmargs governs the buildSrc daemon specifically because that daemon starts before the plain kotlin.daemon.jvmargs property is read.

jvmDefault's default is now ENABLE (not just renamed from -Xjvm-default) per the live gradle-compiler-options.html table — confirmed independently by two exemplars (shadow, detekt) explicitly overriding it back to NO_COMPATIBILITY, implying real projects are already compensating for the flip.

WebFetch's small-model summarization of kotlinlang.org pages was unreliable for flag-name precision (e.g. mangled '-Xwhen-guards' into '-Xguard-conditions' in one summary) — cross-checking whatsnew21 vs whatsnew22 vs the live compiler-reference.html was necessary to get exact flag identity right.

extraWarnings/-Wextra has now sat at Experimental for four consecutive minor releases (2.1.0 through 2.4.0) with zero stabilization signal in any fetched whatsnew page — longer than typical for a Kotlin experimental feature, worth flagging as possibly stalled rather than just 'still cooking'.

rule_ids: JAVA-PLAT-01 — State toolchain JDK and bytecode floor as two explicit values; express the floor as options.release / maven.compiler.release, never sourceCompatibility/<source>/<target> alone (MUST)
JAVA-PLAT-02 — Declare the OCX SDK at floor 17, toolchain 25, CI matrix 17/21/25 (MUST, SDK)
JAVA-PLAT-03 — Confirm the toolchain is JDK 22+ any vendor, or 21.0.8+/17.0.19+ OpenJDK-family with -XDaddTypeAnnotationsToSymbol=true, before setting NullAway jspecifyMode; never Oracle 17/21 (MUST)
JAVA-PLAT-04 — Ship a real module-info.java with a minimal exports list; use Automatic-Module-Name only below floor 9 and never call it encapsulation (MUST for SDK/library, CONSIDER for app/CLI)
JAVA-PLAT-05 — When the floor is below 9, compile module-info.java in a dedicated release-9+ execution and exclude it from the base compile (MUST when floor < 9)
JAVA-PLAT-06 — Declare every --add-opens/--add-exports per module at the point of use with a comment naming the library; never a global relax flag (MUST)
JAVA-PLAT-07 — Run jdeps --jdk-internals -R and jdeprscan --for-removal before raising a JDK major and treat any hit as blocking (MUST)

JAVA-PLAT-08 — Before crossing JDK 21, grep every List/Deque/Set/Map/Collection implementor for self-declared getFirst/getLast/addFirst/addLast/removeFirst/removeLast/reversed and re-check var-typed inference (SHOULD)
JAVA-PLAT-09 — Carry the exact JDK number on every removal/disablement claim (Security Manager 24, finalization 18, Unsafe warn 24/throw 26+, x86-32 removed 25, Applet removed 26, JNI warn 24) (MUST)
JAVA-PLAT-10 — Never call a charset-less overload; pass an explicit StandardCharsets constant even on a JDK 18+ floor (MUST)
JAVA-PLAT-11 — Sort, or use LinkedHashMap/TreeMap, at the boundary where any golden file, generated source or serialized fixture is produced from a HashMap/HashSet/ServiceLoader (SHOULD)
JAVA-PLAT-12 — Pin options.encoding = "UTF-8" or <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8 explicitly, regardless of JDK floor (MUST)
JAVA-PLAT-13 — Set org.gradle.jvmargs=-Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 in the root gradle.properties whenever a non-UTF-8-default host is in the matrix (MUST conditional, SHOULD otherwise)
JAVA-PLAT-14 — Treat any -Dfile.encoding value other than UTF-8 or COMPAT on a JDK 18+ floor as a defect (MUST)
JAVA-PLAT-15 — Strip Properties.store()'s unconditional date comment from any .properties written into a published artifact, via java.properties.date or a sorted comment-free subclass (SHOULD)
JAVA-PLAT-16 — Declare <project.build.outputTimestamp> explicitly as ISO-8601 UTC on any Maven module claiming reproducibility (SHOULD)
JAVA-PLAT-17 — CONSIDER pinning the test-suite timezone on date/time-sensitive modules; do not raise above CONSIDER without an owner decision (CONSIDER)
JAVA-PLAT-18 — CONSIDER one CI job under a non-English, non-Latin locale for case/format/collation code, the call-site lint being the actual MUST (CONSIDER)
KT-COMP-01 — Never emit -Xwhen-guards, -Xnon-local-break-continue, -Xmulti-dollar-interpolation (retired 2.2.0) or -Xcontext-parameters (retired 2.4.0); -Xcontext-receivers is always a defect (MUST)
KT-COMP-02 — Never write -Xjvm-default= as a string flag; use the typed compilerOptions.jvmDefault property (MUST)
KT-COMP-03 — State compilerOptions.jvmDefault explicitly on any library or SDK publishing Kotlin interfaces on 2.2.0+, because the default flipped to ENABLE (MUST for library/SDK)
KT-COMP-04 — Set compilerOptions.jvmTarget explicitly alongside jvmToolchain(N), and make it equal the Java side's options.release in a mixed module (MUST)
KT-COMP-05 — Do not weaken jvmTargetValidationMode from its ERROR default without a comment naming why (MUST)
KT-COMP-06 — Check the KGP/Gradle/AGP compatibility table before bumping either, and bump KGP in the same change when a Gradle bump crosses its ceiling (MUST)
KT-COMP-07 — Never emit K1-era advice; -language-version 1.8/1.9 was dropped in Kotlin 2.3.0 and K1 itself removed in 2.4.0, and a claim must name which (MUST)
KT-COMP-08 — Use KSP in any new Kotlin module needing an annotation processor; kapt only with a comment naming the processor that lacks a KSP implementation (MUST)
KT-COMP-09 — Do not split one processor's inputs across kapt(...) and ksp(...) in the same module (MUST)
KT-COMP-10 — Do not set ksp.useKSP2=false on KSP >= 2.3.0 or AGP >= 9.0 (MUST)
KT-COMP-11 — Pin Dokka >= 2.2.0 and configure it through the DGP v2 top-level dokka {} extension, not v1 per-task shapes (SHOULD)
KT-COMP-12 — Treat extraWarnings / -Wextra as opt-in and say so; never a MUST while it stays Experimental (CONSIDER)
KT-COMP-13 — Put Kotlin daemon JVM args at the level the target daemon reads; buildSrc reads -Dkotlin.daemon.jvm.options inside org.gradle.jvmargs (SHOULD)
conflicts_resolved: Timezone pinning severity: map row M-Q-06 ranks it P0/P1 while the encoding dive keeps it CONSIDER. Resolved CONSIDER — priority ranks research value, severity ranks what fails a build, and 0/32 corpus support cannot carry a MUST (jvm-quality-gates.md verdict 10 names this exact rule as the one agents invent).

JAVA-PLAT-01's verification: the jdk-floors dive wrote it as a grep-and-flag on sourceCompatibility/<source>/<target>. That flags guava, whose 1.8 base layer is CORRECT as the base of a two-execution MR-JAR. Resolved: the check reads the owning compile task/<execution> for a governing release value — the same correction wave-2 #33 applied to GRADLE-DEP-05.

Adversarial-locale CI job: the encoding dive rated it SHOULD (2/32). Demoted to CONSIDER with a reason the dive did not give — the MUST that actually catches locale defects is the call-site lint (-Xep:StringCaseLocaleUsage:ERROR, DefaultLocale) owned by JAVA-LINT; the CI job is the residual.

jvmTarget vs options.release: the jdk-floors dive owns the Java floor knob and the Kotlin dive owns jvmTarget, and neither states the joint rule for a mixed Java+Kotlin module. Resolved into one rule (KT-COMP-04): the two are one decision written twice, with jvmTargetValidationMode (default ERROR) as the enforcement, plus the explicit caveat that a Kotlin-only module never triggers the validator.

Kotlin floor, two conflated facts: frame correction 2 says Kotlin 2.4.0 ends K1 outright; the Kotlin dive cites whatsnew23 that -language-version 1.8/1.9 was dropped in 2.3.0. Both true and different — language-version values died at 2.3.0, the K1 compiler at 2.4.0. KT-COMP-07 requires a claim to name which.

Archive-reproducibility scope: the encoding dive proposed DET-05/DET-06 as rules that mostly point at GRADLE-CACHE-17. Resolved: they are not rules in this family. JAVA-PLAT keeps only what Gradle's archive defaults cannot reach (Properties.store(), Maven outputTimestamp, mergeServiceFiles()'s classpath ordering); kafka's live opt-out is restated as evidence, not re-ruled.

japicmp rule ownership: the jdk-floors dive proposed JAVA-PLAT-08/09 (bind to check/verify; flat accepted-breaks file). Those belong to JAVA-API/JAVA-LINT, already consolidated in wave 2. Resolved: the six-repo re-measurement and the copyable templates are handed back as evidence rather than duplicated as JAVA-PLAT rules.

NullAway jspecifyMode rule ownership vs JAVA-LINT-05 in jvm-quality-gates.md: resolved by splitting on who breaks it — JAVA-LINT-05 owns the lint wiring, JAVA-PLAT-03 owns the toolchain-and-vendor precondition, because the agent editing the toolchain block is the one who trips it.

Kover check wiring: the Kotlin dive settled that check DOES depend on koverVerify by default since 0.7.0 (opposite of JaCoCo), proven by a task tree and a maintainer's onCheck=false fix, while Kover's own current docs still never state it. Resolved as a correction handed to JAVA-TEST-08, not as a KT-COMP rule, to avoid a duplicated rule across families.

Dokka's home: the Kotlin dive rates it a KT-COMP rule while M-Y-06 says docs-quality's generator table has no shape for Dokka. Resolved by splitting — the version-and-DSL rule is KT-COMP (it edits *.gradle.kts); only the unsolved tested-examples/generator-row gap goes to the sibling set as a file edit.
needs_another_round: Mixed-module bytecode floor (KT-COMP/JAVA-PLAT boundary) — in a multi-project library, what mechanically enforces one bytecode floor across a Kotlin-only module and a Java-only module whose compile tasks never meet, given jvmTargetValidationMode only fires when both exist in the same module?

Dokka in docs-quality (M-Y-06) — does Dokka get a new row in the sibling set's wiring-by-generator.md and tested-examples-by-language.md, or does the JVM set carry its own subprocess-harness rule for tested doc examples? Sibling-file edit either way, not a new artifact.

Properties.store() on the Gradle side — is there any supported Gradle-side mechanism equivalent to Maven's java.properties.date, or must every plugin writing .properties output re-implement Shadow's ReproducibleProperties?
JEP 472 JNI deny-by-default — has a target JDK release been announced since 2026-09-12? JDK 24 ships warn and the JEP promises only 'a future release', so no rule may name a number today.

CI-runner timezone audit (JAVA-PLAT-17's decider) — do the CI runners the corpus actually uses default to UTC? That measurement is what separates '0/32 because nobody needs it' from '0/32 because nobody looked', and it is the only thing that can move the rule off CONSIDER in either direction.

top_rules: JAVA-SEC-01: never call ObjectInputStream.readObject()/readUnshared() on a boundary-crossing stream without an attached ObjectInputFilter allow-list; automate via Error Prone BanSerializableRead (ERROR)

JAVA-SEC-02: any Jackson polymorphic typing must resolve to jackson-databind ≥2.18.8/≥2.21.4/≥3.1.4 with an explicit PolymorphicTypeValidator — 'a validator exists' is not the check, 'the validator is patched against CVE-2026-54512/54513' is

JAVA-SEC-03: harden every XML factory type independently (DocumentBuilderFactory, SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory, TransformerFactory, SchemaFactory, Validator, JAXB, XPath) — hardening one is not evidence for another, and none of this is in core SpotBugs

JAVA-SEC-04: never pass attacker-influenced strings to Context.lookup() or ~40 related JNDI/JDO/JMX/SQL-rowset APIs; automate via Error Prone BanJNDI (ERROR) — no dedicated CERT rule number exists, cite CERT VU#930724 instead

JAVA-SEC-05: every archive-extraction loop must resolve+normalize each entry path and verify containment against the destination root before writing — the JDK ships no safe extraction API for zip/tar/jar/war/apk/7z

JAVA-SEC-07: build subprocess commands with array/varargs ProcessBuilder only, never concatenation or 'sh -c' — binds the OCX SDK's own process-launch code; 5/5 measured corpus call sites already do this correctly

JAVA-SEC-09: SpotBugs earns a place in this gate only paired with find-sec-bugs, scoped to untrusted-input modules — measured find-sec-bugs 0/32, and all 3 corpus SpotBugs users (kafka, assertj, spotless) run without it

JAVA-SEC-10: never cite Oracle's Secure Coding Guidelines section 9 (ACCESS-1..20) as live guidance for JDK-24+ targets — JEP 486 disabled the Security Manager and Oracle's own page now carries that disclaimer on every guideline in the section
surprises: Oracle's own seccodeguide.html has already been edited for JDK 24: all 20 Access Control guidelines (9-1..9-20) carry a verbatim 'security manager permanently disabled since Java 24' note — the source resolves its own currency problem, it doesn't need to be excluded wholesale.

CVE-2026-54512 and CVE-2026-54513 are two distinct bypass mechanisms in one advisory (generic-parameter substring check vs allowIfSubTypeIsArray() component check), not one bug — patching one code path does not close the other; only a version bump fixes both.

There is no CERT rule numbered specifically for JNDI lookups; the closest (IDS54-J) only covers the LDAP-query half. The operative primary sources are Error Prone's BanJNDI and CERT/CC's VU#930724, not a SEI IDS-category rule.

top_rules: Never let a caught InterruptedException (directly or via a broader catch) fall through without re-interrupting or propagating — promote disabled InterruptedExceptionSwallowed, since the on-by-default InterruptedInCatchBlock catches a different mistake
Never catch Throwable/Error except at a documented top-level boundary — Error Prone TryFailThrowable (on by default) for tests, SonarJava S1181 for production
Promote -Xep:CatchingUnchecked:ERROR -Xep:UnusedException:ERROR explicitly — both are DISABLED_CHECKS and are the two most characteristic agent-written swallow/sever shapes

Any Closeable/AutoCloseable including Files.walk/list/lines/find streams must be acquired in try-with-resources — verify via StreamResourceLeak+MustBeClosedChecker (Error Prone, on by default) or S2095 (SonarJava), never PMD CloseResource (deprecated by S2095, 0/32 enforced)
Never wrap a caught exception as new X(e.getMessage()) — always pass the original as cause; verify with UnusedException plus a direct grep for the .getMessage()-in-constructor shape

Don't rely on SonarJava S4507 alone for printStackTrace/System.exit — it reports as a Security Hotspot invisible to a default Issues-only gate; use Error Prone's on-by-default CatchAndPrintStackTrace instead

On a project already running Error Prone+NullAway, still run SpotBugs CORRECTNESS+MT_CORRECTNESS — UL_UNRELEASED_LOCK and the annotation-free NP_* null-dataflow family have no Error Prone equivalent at all

Before treating any SpotBugs/PMD declaration as a real gate, confirm it's bound to the build's failure path (Gradle ignoreFailures=false plus check/test.dependsOn, or Maven <build><plugins> with an invoked goal) — a Maven <reporting>-only block with no `mvn site` CI job never fails a build, as assertj's own SpotBugs declaration demonstrates
